parsed.summary: For every ν > 0, the two theorems assert Fefferman's breakdown alternatives. (C): there are smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u₀ and f on ℝ³ such that no smooth (v,p) on ℝ³×[0,∞) solves Navier–Stokes with v(·,t) ∈ L² and uniformly bounded energy. (D): the same on the torus, with no smooth spatially 1-periodic solution. This matches the 'Consequently…' part of Theorem 1.1 and the final sentence of Corollary 10.6. The main caveat is in (D): the pressure must also be 1-periodic. That is an extra requirement inside the ¬∃ and makes the statement weaker, though it follows the Clay errata and the paper's periodic pressure P_per. The blow-up construction itself (compact support, L∞ blow-up as t↑1) is not formalized.

glossary.plain: ∇·v(x) = trace of the Jacobian Dv(x); equals 0 where v is not differentiable
glossary.note: Junk value only at non-differentiable points; every use is on smooth fields.

glossary.plain: f(x+e_i) = f(x) for all x and every coordinate i
In addition, for all m and all real K there is C with ‖D^m u₀(x)‖ ≤ C(1+|x|)^{-K}
glossary.note: Allowing K < 0 is a vacuous strengthening; the base is ≥ 1, so there is no junk division.

glossary.plain: Every space-time derivative of f is bounded by C(1+|x|+t)^{-K} for t ≥ 0
f(·,t) is 1-periodic for t ≥ 0, and every derivative is bounded by C(1+t)^{-K}
(v,p) satisfy, for t ≥ 0: ∂_t v + (v·∇)v = νΔv − ∇p + f (one-sided time derivative); ∇·v = 0; v(·,0) = u₀; v and p are C^∞ on ℝⁿ×[0,∞)
In addition, v(·,t) ∈ L² for each t ≥ 0 and sup_t ∫|v|² < E for some E
glossary.note: The MemLp hypothesis makes the Bochner integral genuine, not a junk 0.

glossary.plain: In addition, v(·,t) and p(·,t) are 1-periodic for t ≥ 0
glossary.standard_concept: Fefferman condition (10) plus the errata on pressure periodicity
glossary.note: Pressure periodicity is not in Fefferman's original (10). It is the errata and standard fix, and matches the paper's P_per.

lean_claims.plain: For all ν > 0 there exist u₀, f: ℝ³ → ℝ³ (f time-dependent) such that u₀ is smooth, divergence-free and Schwartz-decaying, f is smooth on ℝ³×[0,∞) with all derivatives O((1+|x|+t)^{-K}), and there are no v, p that are smooth on ℝ³×[0,∞) and satisfy NS, ∇·v = 0, v(·,0) = u₀, v(·,t) ∈ L² for every t ≥ 0, and sup_{t≥0} ‖v(t)‖²_{L²} < ∞.

For all ν > 0 there exist smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic u₀ and smooth, spatially 1-periodic f with all derivatives O((1+t)^{-K}), such that there are no smooth v, p on ℝ³×[0,∞) satisfying NS, ∇·v = 0, v(·,0) = u₀, with both v(·,t) and p(·,t) 1-periodic for every t ≥ 0.

paper_claims.plain: For every ν > 0 there exist f ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ³×(0,∞)), a compact set K, and smooth u, p on ℝ³×[0,1) solving NS with u(·,0) = 0, supported in K, with bounded L² norm and limsup_{t↑1} ‖u‖_∞ = ∞. Consequently there is no smooth solution on ℝ³×[0,∞) with the same data and uniformly bounded kinetic energy, i.e. alternative (C).

For every ν > 0 there is a smooth force on 𝕋³×[0,∞), compactly supported in time, such that the periodic solution (U, P_per) with zero data blows up in L∞ as t↑1. There is no global smooth periodic solution for the same data, i.e. alternative (D).

coverage.why: Lean asserts Fefferman's (C); the paper's data (u₀ = 0, compactly supported f) are admissible witnesses.

coverage.paper_ref: Theorem 1.1 (blow-up construction, compact support, L∞ blow-up)
coverage.why: Only the non-existence consequence is stated.
Matches (D) with periodic pressure, consistent with the paper's P_per and the Clay errata. It is weaker than a literal reading of Fefferman's original (10).

flags.explanation: The solution must also have 1-periodic pressure. This is an extra requirement inside ¬∃, so the breakdown claim is weaker than Fefferman's original (D), which constrains only u. It follows the Clay errata and the paper's periodic pressure P_per. Without it, solutions with non-periodic pressure (e.g. a spatially constant velocity g(t) with p = −g'(t)·x) could exist.
flags.probe_idea: State a variant without isOnePeriodic_pressure and compare. The constant-velocity/linear-pressure example shows the field is necessary for a meaningful (D).

flags.explanation: The paper's main content (an explicit smooth solution on [0,1) with compact support, bounded energy, and L∞ blow-up) is not formalized. Only the non-existence consequence is.

The time derivative is derivWithin on Ici 0 (one-sided at t = 0), and smoothness is ContDiffOn on univ ×ˢ Ici 0. This is a faithful encoding of C^∞(ℝ³×[0,∞)). Because v and p are required smooth, the fderiv, Δ and gradient terms are never junk.

lint_verdicts.why: Divergence is only applied to fields required to be C^∞, so fderiv is genuine.
u₀ is required ContDiff ∞, so iteratedFDeriv is the true derivative.
velocity_smooth on univ ×ˢ Ici 0 makes the spatial and one-sided time derivatives genuine for t ≥ 0.
The integrable field (MemLp ‖v·t‖ 2) guarantees ‖v‖² is integrable, so the integral is the true energy.
The base 1+‖x‖ ≥ 1, so the rpow is positive and there is no division by zero.
